chapter: Virginia school and first Washington bands
title: Manager Bailey's fifty cents, Tommy Miles's beans, and the Howard pit band
summary: The manager Bailey paid the band fifty cents each; Miles fed them at home; they played the Club Prudome and the Howard Theater pit.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: And Bailey used to manage this band. And he'd book us on jobs, and man, he'd tell us, oh, we didn't make much money tonight. He'd give us fifty cents apiece, something like that, and maybe he sold the band, 13 pieces, for $150.00. Fifty cents. We talked about that and we laughed, and everytime I see Eckstine that's a standing joke. Bailey's been dead a long time. Did you see Bailey. You know, did you see Bailey. Ah, yeah, Bailey was -- he was something else, man.

And anyway, Tommy was a nice guy, Tommy Miles. A lot of times we didn't have any money. We were kids and no money to eat with. But Tommy went home, he would have his wife cook up a big pot of beans or something like that. And he'd feed us, you know, over at his house. And we'd rehearse all the time because the guys liked to rehearse.
And we were working on -- we were working on a job there, the Club Prudome. And we must have stayed there about a year, a little longer than a year at that club. And then

we used to play shows at the Howard Theater. We'd go in there, you know, like -- and just play in the pit. We didn't go nothing on the stage because we weren't that good to feature too much on the stage.
Wasn't there a steady house band at the Howard?
We were there. We were a steady house band --
